title: I built a co-op dark fantasy roguelite with Claude, then ran 2,000+ headless sim runs to balance it. Now I need real players to prove the sims wrong.
author: ThePacerfan-12
selftext:
**Hollowmarch** is a turn-based dark fantasy roguelite that runs in the browser. Think of it as a randomized D&D one-shot: three acts, a branching board, a boss at the end of each act.  
Works on desktop and phone with no download. Link players run solo with up to four AI companions, which you add in the lobby.  
**What's in it**  
8 classes (Knight, Cleric, Witch, Cutpurse, Plague Doctor, Hunter, Penitent, Gravecaller)  
D&D-style encounters where you roll a d20 against your stats  
Party turns: everyone picks an action, then the turn resolves by Speed  
Oaths you swear for blessings and break for curses, a secret fourth act, skill upgrades, item sets and keystone relics  
A 3D diorama for every scene  
**How it was made**  
I designed and directed it; Claude wrote the code (three.js, a turn-based sim, host-authoritative co-op). The project rule is open-source assets only, so every model, texture, sound and track is CC0 or public domain: KayKit and Quaternius models, Poly Haven textures, engravings from The Met's open-access collection, and music from OpenGameArt. Credits are in-game.  
The part I'm proudest of is balancing by simulation. We ran the game's own battle code headless in Node, with AI "personas" (planner, rusher, newcomer) playing thousands of runs. That caught things I'd never have found by hand: a 5,900-turn stalemate, a bug where one action silently broke an oath, and AI teammates that never used half their skills. Class balance went from a 24–79% solo win spread to 51–66%.  
**Where I need you**  
Sims can tell me whether a class wins. They can't tell me whether it's fun, so I'm looking for:  
Was picking a hero and starting a run clear?  
Where did you die, and did it feel fair or cheap?  
Did any choice feel pointless?  
Did you want "one more run"?  
The end-of-run screen has a short notes form and a button that emails me your run log. The log contains game actions only, nothing personal. A comment here helps just as much. I'll answer anything about the process too.
